evidence: All 52 criterion descriptions were read (gates 2, functional 40, polish 5, visual 5). Every binary criterion states a positive bar, then explicit 'Fails if ...' clauses, then the uniform catch-all 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold.' The catch-all folds any narrower explicit fail list into one conjunctive full-credit bar, so no criterion lists requirements and then waives most of them. The clauses that relax a requirement are scoped alternatives that keep the same bar, not waivers that create a second target. Examples: render gate hro_gate_render, 'a refusal message is welcome but not required' (gates/render/judge.toml:23). Functional rows: 'hiding it is optional' in hro_move_one_stage (functional/judge.toml:56), hro_reject_hired (:92) and hro_mgr_other_job (:164). hro_refused_put_back (:137): 'A UI that refuses before the card moves, with the reason shown and focus on that card, also passes', which keeps the same reason and focus bar. hro_observer_readonly (:173), 'Whether the Observer's screens show such controls is the app's choice'. hro_candidate_private (:389), board and Activity reads 'refused or answered with only that candidate's own data'. hro_pol_session_resume (polish/judge.toml:59), 'unless the sign-in prompt has already appeared on its own (that also passes)'. The ownership notes hand an observable to exactly one sibling and narrow nothing inside the row: hro_arrive_bottom to hro_bulk_move, hro_interview_full to hro_bulk_places/hro_undo_full, hro_candidate_view to hro_msg_exchange, and hro_candidate_linked. Several rows bundle multiple promises, such as hro_pol_failed_send (failed send plus a note draft surviving a reload) and hro_pol_session_resume. They still name one conjunctive bar, and the skill lists this as a known false positive for check 33; whether those promises should earn separate credit belongs to checks 26/28 under REVIEW_POLICY 'Independent credit takes precedence over flow grouping', not to this row. The 5 visual criteria are likert, each with one anchor ladder (1-5), and have no competing bar. The instances below are reported because the row says to report every instance. Neither one creates two targets inside a single criterion description. Each comes from wording that differs between a criterion and its prompt or protocol, or from a fail clause missing from the positive list, and a conforming app satisfies both readings. (1) hro_activity (functional/judge.toml:263) grades 'every successful action you performed on J1 and J2', but protocol A (functional/prompt.md:49) limits it to actions 'in S, M, L, C, B and R'. The listed run order puts T (Tomas card added to J2), K (Tomas's J2 card moved, rejected and reopened) and V (Mei's J1 move and add) before A, so the criterion's set is larger than the protocol's. (2) Protocol R (functional/prompt.md:45) tells the judge to 'confirm no move, add or note control is offered' for Aud and Tomas. hro_observer_readonly (:173) and the general protocol rule (prompt.md:23, 'Whether a refused action is offered at all is the app's choice') say that showing controls is not graded, so the 'confirm' step reads as a requirement the criterion then waives. (3) hro_pol_live_thread (polish/judge.toml:32): the positive bar lists draft text, focus and appending, while the fail clause adds 'the view moves away from the newest message'. The next sentence, 'This row owns the draft and focus', could be read as dropping the view requirement, but the catch-all and hireops_rules.md:158 ('if they are at the newest message, it is shown') make the view requirement part of the bar. Run evidence: none needed for this source-level row. No judge run was consulted, and nothing here claims an Oracle, model or portal score.
counterexample: Weak app that could pass: an app that logs S/M/L/C/B/R actions but not later additions or moves (for example, candidate-email-linked additions in T or moves by Mei in V). A judge following protocol A's list passes hro_activity, while one following the criterion's 'every successful action you performed on J1 and J2' fails it. The two readings disagree only for such an app. Conforming app that could fail: an app that shows server-refused move, add and note controls to the Observer, which public rules allow ('changes nothing', hireops_rules.md:18/73), could lose hro_observer_readonly if the judge treats protocol R's 'confirm no ... control is offered' as graded, despite the criterion's explicit waiver. Both risks are low because a correct golden-style app logs every action and the criterion text controls.
suggested_fix: Optional tightening, not blocking: in protocol A, replace 'in S, M, L, C, B and R' with 'in every protocol before A (S, M, L, C, B, N, T, U, K, R, V)', or narrow hro_activity to the same list. In protocol R, change 'confirm no move, add or note control is offered' to 'record whether move, add or note controls are offered (not graded)'. In hro_pol_live_thread, add 'the view stays at the newest message showing Noor's message' to the positive list.
